232:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to willfully and intentionally violate any of the sections of this article.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to dump or bury or to cause to be dumped or buried any garbage, refuse, rubbish, or brown and white goods anywhere in the unincorporated area of the county.
(c) No solid waste may be disposed of by any person in an open dump, nor may any person cause, suffer, allow or permit open dumping on his property.
(d) No owner or occupant shall allow the accumulation on premises under his control or on or about his residential unit or commercial establishment of solid waste or scrap tires where the accumulation of such solid waste or scrap tires creates or may create a health hazard to neighbors or other citizens, is unsightly, or emits foul or obnoxious odors which constitute either a public or private nuisance or is in violation of state law.
(e) It shall be unlawful for any person to willfully and with intent to defraud the county or its designated contract collector, to evade or defeat or attempt to evade or defeat any fee, charge, penalty or interest due the county or its contract collector or the payment thereof imposed by this article.
(f) It shall be unlawful for any person to burn or attempt to burn or cause to be burned any material of any nature in any container belonging to or used by the county or its designated contract collector for residential solid waste collection purposes.
(g) It shall be unlawful for any person to willfully and intentionally damage or destroy or to allow or permit damage to or destruction of any container provided by the county or its designated contract collector.
(h) Each violation of any of the sections of this article shall, upon conviction be punishable as provided in section 18-115. Such violations may be tried upon citations with or without a prosecuting attorney as well as upon accusations as provided in O.C.G.A. § 15-10-60 et seq. Service upon corporations, partnerships and other entities and organizations shall be effective by serving any managing agent located in the county or by serving the registered agent or any officer or partner of the corporation, partnership, organization or entity. This article may also be enforced through other remedies, such as injunctive relief as provided by the laws of this state.
(i) Whenever a corporation, partnership, organization, or other artificial entity shall violate any of the sections of this article, such violation shall be deemed to be that of the individual directors, officers or agents of such corporation, partnership, organization or other artificial entity who shall have authorized, ordered or done any of the acts constituting in whole or in part any such violation. In such cases, service shall also be made upon the individual director or other agent accused of authorizing, ordering or doing acts constituting in whole or in part violations of this article.
( Ord. of 9-12-2006 , att.(54-3))
233:
Any person who violates any part of this section may be charged by citation, or by accusation, to the magistrate court of the county, and upon conviction, shall be punished according to section 1-4.
( Ord. of 9-12-2006 )
236:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Commercial solid waste means all types of solid waste generated by stores, offices, restaurants, warehouses, and other non-manufacturing activities, excluding residential and industrial waste.
Industrial waste means solid waste generated by manufacturing or industrial processes or operations that is not a hazardous waste regulated under the state Hazardous Waste Management Act. Such waste includes, but is not limited to, waste resulting from the following manufacturing processes: electric power generations; fertilizer and agricultural chemicals; food-related products and byproducts; inorganic chemicals, iron and steel products; leather and leather products; nonferrous metal and foundry products; organic chemicals, plastics and resins, pulp and paper; rubber and miscellaneous plastic products; stone, glass, clay, and concrete products; textiles; transportation equipment; and water treatment. The term "industrial waste" does not include mining waste or oil and gas waste.
( Ord. of 9-12-2006 , att.(54-71))
237:
County contract collector may contract with businesses, commercial establishments, industrial establishments and others to furnish a dumpster or dumpsters for such business or others use for the collection of applicable waste. All costs for said dumpster shall be born by the person requesting the dumpster.
( Ord. of 9-12-2006 , att.(54-72))
238:
All dumpsters maintained and provided for use by the contract collector shall be for commercial solid waste or industrial waste except in these cases where household garbage is allowed under these ordinances.
( Ord. of 9-12-2006 , att.(54-73))
239:
Violation of this article shall, upon conviction, be punishable as provided in section 18-115.
( Ord. of 9-12-2006 , att.(54-74))
240:
It shall be unlawful for any person who has contracted with the county contract collector for a dumpster to be placed on his or her or its property, to dump any materiel other than commercial solid waste and industrial waste into a dumpster pursuant to an agreement between the person with the dumpster and the county contract collector, except in those cases where household garbage is allowed by this article.
( Ord. of 9-12-2006 , att.(54-75))
241:
No person shall dump, deposit, or place any trash, garbage, or other such materials at a dumpster site maintained by the county contract collector for use by the person contracting with county contract collector at any place other than totally within the dumpster container.
( Ord. of 9-12-2006 , att.(54-76))
242:
No person shall enter, reach into, scavenge from, or remove any contents from a garbage or trash dumpster maintained by the county and/or the county contract collector.
( Ord. of 9-12-2006 , att.(54-77))
243:
No person shall loiter upon, park, stand, or remain on the premises of any dumpster site maintained by the county contract collector, except the person who contracts with the county contract collector to have a dumpster on his or her or its premises, or their family, agents, servants, employees or representatives.
( Ord. of 9-12-2006 , att.(54-78))
244:
Any person who violates any part of this article may be charged by citation, or by accusation, to the magistrate court of Marion County, Georgia, and, upon conviction, shall be fined a fine from $125.00 to $500.00 and/or sentenced to the county jail for a period up to 60 days. Each day of violation shall be a new and separate offense.
( Ord. of 9-12-2006 , att.(54-91))
247:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Public or private property means the right-of-way of any road or highway; any body of water or watercourse or the shores or beaches thereof; any park, playground, building, refuge or conservation or recreation area; and residential or farm properties, timberlands or forests.
Scrap tire means a tire that is no longer suitable for its original intended purpose because of wear, damage or defect.
Scrap tire carrier means any person engaged in picking up or transporting scrap tires, not otherwise exempted under Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. R. 391-3-4-.19(5)(g), for the purpose of removal to a scrap tire processor, end user or disposal facility.
Scrap tire generator means any person who generates scrap tires as defined in Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. R. 391-3-4-.19(2)(m).
Tire retailer means any person engaged in business of selling new replacement tires.
( Ord. No. 09082009 , 9-8-2009)
248:
Any person, firm or corporation violating any portion of this article shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, in the magistrate court of the county, shall be punished as follows and according to section 1-4.
(1) By fine of not less than $100.00 nor more than $1,000.00 or up to 60 days imprisonment, or both. Each day the violation continues shall be a separate offense. However, This subsection shall not preclude the county from choosing to see civil redress in a court of competent jurisdiction in addition to the criminal prosecution, it being the intent of the county to have both the civil and criminal rights of prosecution in this area; and/or
(2) The court may order the publication of the names of persons convicted of violating this article.
If any person, whether owner, tenant, agent or employee, owning, holding or occupying property in the county shall fail or refuse to clean up said scrap tire material from such property, within ten days written notice addressed to the owner of said property and delivered to said property by a county official or employee with a copy mailed by certified mail to the owner of said property as shown on the tax digest of the county, the county may remove the scrap tire material from said property. Such matter shall be done at the expense of the owner of said property. Upon completion of such work, execution shall be issued upon application by the county by the magistrate court of the county against said owner and against said property for such expense and all costs. The person returning such property for taxation in the county, or the person against whom said property may be assessed in the event there has been no return of such property by the owner of same, shall be deemed to be the true owner of said property.
( Ord. No. 09082009 , 9-8-2009)
249:
(a) The owner or occupant of any premises shall be responsible for the sanitary handling and disposing of all scrap tires on the premises used or occupied by such person.
(b) It shall be unlawful to dump or permit the dumping of scrap tires at any place in the county, including, without limitations, any public or private property in the county or any waters in the county unless:
(1) The property is designated by the board of commissioners or its duly designated agent for the disposal of scrap tires and the person is authorized to use such property;
(2) The scrap tire is placed into a receptacle or container installed specifically for such property; or
(3) The person is the owner or tenant in lawful possession of such property or has first obtained consent of the owner or tenant in lawful possession or unless the act is done under the personal direction of the owner or tenant, all in a manner consistent with the public welfare and not otherwise in violation of law.
(c) All persons defined as scrap tire generators, scrap tire carriers or tire retailers shall comply with the provisions of Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. R. 391-3-4-.19, and shall handle scrap tires in accordance with the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 12-8-20 et seq., and Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. ch. 391-3-4, applicable to scrap tires.
( Ord. No. 09082009 , 9-8-2009)
250:
The following regulations apply to scrap tires:
(1) No person shall deposit a scrap tire in any container or receptacle unless authorized by the owner of the receptacle or the county commissioners or their designee.
(2) No person shall deposit any burning or smoldering material in such container or receptacle.
(3) No person shall set fire to the contents of any such container or receptacle.
(4) No person shall deposit any flammable or explosive materials in any such container or receptacle.
(5) No dead animals shall be deposited in any such container or receptacle.
(6) No person shall willfully damage or alter the location of any such container or receptacle without the written consent of the board of commissioners.
(7) No salvage or scavenging operations shall be conducted in or around such containers or receptacles except by written consent of the board of commissioners.
( Ord. No. 09082009 , 9-8-2009)
251:
Enforcement of this article shall be the responsibility of the county board of commissioners or its designee or the county sheriff's office or her/her designee. Any person or persons authorized to enforce this article shall be empowered to enter any property, upon reasonable cause, at reasonable times in order to inspect the property for violations of this article, subject to the condition that to allow entry on private property for inspection, the alleged violation of this article must be visible from a public road or right-of-way, or upon such officer having received a complaint by a resident of the county alleging a violation of this article. The magistrate court of the county shall also be authorized to issue summons for hearing on alleged violation of the article upon written accusation of any person sui juris alleging such violation.
( Ord. No. 09082009 , 9-8-2009)
256:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Billboard means any outdoor advertising sign.
Public road means any county maintained road located in the county.
( Ord. No. 1-2000 , § I, 1-11-2000)
257:
All billboards located within the county on a public road shall not exceed 70 feet in height. Said distance shall be measured from the ground to the highest point of the billboard.
( Ord. No. 1-2000 , § II, 1-11-2000)
258:
The board of commissioners authorized to adopt this article to ensure that vehicle drivers maintain visual contact with the roadway and traffic, as well as, to provide a greater environmental benefit.
( Ord. No. 1-2000 , § III, 1-11-2000)
259:
To the extent it does not conflict with state law, a violation of the provisions of this article shall be a misdemeanor punishable by fine not to exceed $500.00 or 60 days in jail, or both. Citations for violations shall be returnable to the probate court of the county.
( Ord. No. 1-2000 , § IV, 1-11-2000)
262:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Through traffic means the use of said roadways for all traffic other then pick up or delivery.
Truck means semitrailer, tractor, trailer or truck tractor, or any combination thereof as defined in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1.
( Ord. No. 12-98(2) , § I, 12-8-1998)
263:
No truck, as defined herein, shall use the county roads as adopted by the board from time to time, according to the current system of numbering, for any through traffic, except for pick up and delivery on any of said roads.
( Ord. No. 12-98(2) , § II, 12-8-1998; Ord. No. 2-99(1) , § II, 2-9-1999)
264:
The board of commissioners is authorized to adopt this article pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 34-4-2(10) as an act necessary, proper and incidental to the efficient operation of the county road system.
( Ord. No. 12-98(2) , § III, 12-8-1998)
265:
To the extent it does not conflict with state law, a violation of the provisions of this article shall be a misdemeanor punishable according to section 1-4.
( Ord. No. 12-98(2) , § IV, 12-8-1998)
268:
All persons or firms harvesting standing timber in any unincorporated area of the county for delivery as pulpwood, logs, poles, posts, or wood chips to any woodyard or processing plant located inside or outside this state shall provide notice of such harvesting operations to the county governing authority or the designated agent thereof prior to entering onto the property if possible, but in no event later than 24 hours after entering onto the property. Further, such persons shall give notice of cessation of cutting within 24 hours after the job is completed.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 1, 2-9-2021)
269:
The notice of harvesting operations required by this article shall be provided for each separate tract to be harvested. Such notice shall be made in such form as prescribed by rule or regulation of the director of the state forestry commission, and shall include the following information:
(1) A map of the area which identifies the location of the tract to be harvested and, as to those trucks which will be traveling to and from such tract for purposes of picking up and hauling loads of cut forest products, the main point of ingress to such tract from a public road and, if different, the main point of egress from such tract to a public road. If multiple points of ingress and/or egress will be used, all such points shall be identified.
(2) A statement as to whether the timber will be removed pursuant to a lump sum sale, per unit sale, or owner harvest for purposes of ad valorem taxation under O.C.G.A. § 48-5-7.5;
(3) The name, address, and daytime telephone number of the timber seller if the harvest is pursuant to a lump sum or per unit sale or of the timber owner if the harvest is an owner harvest; and
(4) The name, business address, business telephone number, and nighttime or emergency telephone number of the person or firm harvesting such timber.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 2, 2-9-2021)
270:
Subject to the provisions of section 20-80, the notice required by this article may be submitted in person, by transmission of an electronic record via telefacsimile or e-mail, or by mail.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 3, 2-9-2021)
271:
Subject to the provisions of section 20-80, upon notification published by the director of the state forestry commission that a statewide notification website or platform is available for public use, persons or firms wishing to utilize said website or platform to provide the notice required by this article may do so at their option, and the county will accept notifications submitted in this manner.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 4, 2-9-2021)
272:
On and after a date specified and published by the director of the state forestry commission, use of the statewide notification website or platform shall be mandatory and shall be the sole means of providing the notice required by this article; on and after said date submission of the notice by any of the means listed in section 20-78 shall cease and will no longer be deemed acceptable or in compliance with this article.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 5, 2-9-2021)
273:
The notice required by this article shall not be or remain effective unless and until the person or firm providing such notice has delivered to the governing authority of the county or its designated agent a valid surety bond, executed by a surety corporation authorized to transact business in this state, protecting the county against any damage caused by such person or firm in the amount of $5,000.00; provided, however, that at the option of the person or firm harvesting timber a valid irrevocable letter of credit issued by a bank or savings and loan association, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 7-1-4, in the amount of $5,000.00 may be provided in lieu of a surety bond. Such bonds or letters of credit shall be subject to the conditions set forth in sections 20-82 and 20-83. No more than one bond or letter of credit shall be required from each person or firm harvesting timber, regardless of the number of tracts harvested in the county for so long as the bond or letter of credit remains in effect. The bond or letter of credit required herein shall be valid only for the calendar year in which it was delivered.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 6, 2-9-2021)
274:
The bond or letter of credit required by section 20-81 shall protect the county against any damage requiring re-ditching or repair of existing ditch structures or the removal of any harvesting residue, including tree tops, debris, logs, pulpwood and other materials, placed in or around the county's rights of way caused by such person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit. The proceeds of such bond or letter of credit shall be available to reimburse the county for any cost incurred to repair such damages or remove such debris in or around the county's rights-of-way. The proceeds of such bond or letter of credit shall also be available to reimburse the county for any costs incurred to maintain or repair county roads damaged by the ingress or egress of motor vehicles engaged in the harvest operations located within 500 feet of any point of ingress or egress of the timber harvesting operation. The right of the county to call such bond or letter of credit in accordance with the provisions of section 20-83 shall be in addition to any other remedies available to the county at law or in equity for damage to county roads or rights-of-way.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 7, 2-9-2021)
275:
When damage results from a person or firm's harvesting activities, the governing authority of the county shall make and provide a written claim to the person or firm causing the damage within 30 business days after the governing authority becomes aware of the damage. Such claim may be given in person, by telefacsimile, email or mail. The claim shall describe the damage in detail and, in compliance with section 20-84(a)(1), give the person or firm the opportunity to repair such damage within 30 days of the notification; provided, however, the county shall be authorized to repair the damage immediately if the governing authority or its designee determines the conditions present a threat to public safety, health or welfare and, upon making such repairs, shall present to the person or firm and the issuer of the applicable bond or letter of credit an itemized list of expenses incurred as a claim against the responsible party and the issuer of its bond or letter of credit. Upon the issuance of a claim as provided in this section the governing authority of the county or its designee shall notify the issuer of the bond or letter of credit that a claim has been made and will be resolved or adjudicated according to the terms of this article.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 8, 2-9-2021)
276:
(a) Within 30 days of receipt of the written claim described in section 20-83, the person or firm against whom the claim is submitted may:
(1) Repair such damage at his or its own expense with the approval and supervision of the governing authority of the county or its designee. When repairs are completed to the satisfaction of the governing authority or its designee, the governing authority or its designee shall provide a written notification of satisfactory completion within five business days to the responsible person or firm and to the surety issuing the bond or the bank issuing the letter of credit, thereby terminating the claim.
(2) In the event of inclement weather or other factors preventing repair of the damage, request a 30-day extension to repair the damage from the governing authority of the county, provided that no extensions shall exceed 90 days from the date the claim was tendered. Approval of any extension shall be at the discretion of the governing authority of the county or its designee.
(3) Appeal the claim to the magistrate court of the county. Any such appeal must name the issuer of the bond or letter of credit as a party, who shall be served with all pleadings in the action and shall have the right to appear. The magistrate court will hear evidence and arguments within 30 days of the written appeal and issue a ruling within ten days of such hearing. Any such appeal shall toll the 30-day period, or any extension thereof, required by section 20-83. If the magistrate court rules in favor of the person or firm against whom the claim was made, the county shall have no right to recover any proceeds of the bond or letter of credit, and judgment shall be entered against the county. If the magistrate court rules in favor of the county the court shall determine the amount of damages to which the county is entitled to recover and enter judgment; accordingly, the governing authority of the county shall be authorized to call the bond or letter of credit and recover from the proceeds thereof an amount equal to the judgment entered by the court, up to the total amount of the bond or letter of credit. The portion of any judgment entered in favor of the county that exceeds the amount of the bond or letter of credit shall be subject to collection by any additional remedies at law or equity.
(b) In the event the person or firm against whom the claim has been submitted fails to take any of the actions allowed under subsection (a)(1), (2) or (3) of this section within the time required therein, such person or firm shall be deemed to have waived any and all rights to contest the call of the bond or letter of credit.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 9, 2-9-2021)
277:
If the person or firm tendering a bond or letter of credit pursuant to the requirements of this article continues its timber harvesting operation beyond the calendar year in which the bond or letter of credit was issued, the person or firm continuing the timber harvesting operation shall tender a new bond or letter of credit within five business days after the first day of the new calendar year.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 10, 2-9-2021)
278:
In the event a bond or letter of credit tendered pursuant to the requirements of this article is revoked by the surety or bank, then a valid replacement bond or letter of credit must be delivered to the governing authority of the county within five business days after the date of revocation in order for timber harvesting operations to continue. In addition, if the person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit caused its revocation, the amount of the bond or letter of credit required shall be increased to $7,500.00 after the first revocation, and $10,000.00 after a second revocation caused by the person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit. The maximum amount of the bond or letter of credit shall not exceed $10,000.00.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 11, 2-9-2021)
279:
Submission of the notice required by this article shall authorize the person or firm submitting same to undertake the timber harvesting operation described in the notice and shall remain in effect until such time as the person or firm gives notice that the harvesting operation is complete; provided, however, that any change in the facts required to be provided for purposes of such notice, including, but not limited to, a change in the scope or extent of the operation, must be reported to the governing authority of the county within three business days after such change.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 12, 2-9-2021)
280:
Any person or firm that engages in a timber harvesting operation in the unincorporated portion of the county without complying with the notice requirements of this article shall be subject to a citation and trial, and upon conviction shall be fined in an amount not to exceed $1,500.00 for each violation.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 13, 2-9-2021)
281:
This article applies to activities which qualify as forestry land management practices or agricultural operations under O.C.G.A. § 12-7-17(5) and (6) on land that is zoned for or used for forestry, silvicultural or agricultural purposes. It shall not authorize land disturbing activities incidental to development in conflict with the limitations set forth in O.C.G.A. § 12-7-17(6).
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 14, 2-9-2021)
282:
Consistent with O.C.G.A. § 12-6-24:
(1) No fee shall be charged to provide and submit the notice required by this article; and
(2) No permit, including a driveway permit, shall be required of the person or firm engaged in a timber harvesting operation as defined by said section. Persons and firms providing the notice required by this article may be asked to consult with county officials responsible for roads and public works for the purpose of minimizing damage to the county's roads, rights of way and infrastructure, and are urged to follow recommendations from county officials. Notwithstanding the forgoing, the person or firm conducting the timber harvest operation bears ultimate responsibility for their actions, and nothing in this article shall preclude the governing authority of the county from taking any and all legal action necessary to protect its property and the health, safety and welfare of its citizens.
( Ord. No. 02092021 , § 15, 2-9-2021)
285:
It is the purpose and intent of this article to ensure that operators engaging in transporting timber or pulpwood harvested in the county be responsible for any damage beyond normal wear and tear inflicted on the county rights-of-way built and maintained to state standards as a result of their operations.
( Ord. No. 01092002 , § II, 1-8-2002)
286:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Access permit means permission to transport timber or pulpwood across county rights-of-way granted by a governing authority. An access permit is required for each harvesting operation, notwithstanding the number of points of ingress and/or egress from that operation.
Applicant means any operator or landowner who files an application to access rights-of-way of the county incident to timber or pulpwood harvesting in the county.
Bond means a surety bond written by a company licensed by the state insurance commissioner or, at the discretion of an applicant, a cash bond, property bond or bank letter of credit.
County rights-of-way means any and all rights-of-way, which are a part of the county road system, delineated in accordance with O.C.G.A. title 32, chapter 4, and intended or used for the passage of motor vehicles by the public.
Damage means any and all injury to the rights-of-way of the county, including, but not be limited to, the following:
(1) Diversion of or the filling in of any drainage ditch, culvert, or pipe parallel to or underneath a county right-of-way, so as to restrain or redirect the flow of water.
(2) The continued ingress or egress, to and from a county right-of-way at a particular location which results in a build-up of rock, gravel, mud, dirt, or other materials, which present hazard to other persons using the county road for authorized purposes.
(3) The operation of any vehicle, machinery, or equipment, which will gouge, rip, break, depress or otherwise deface a public road.
(4) The creation or erection of any dam, berm, ditch, or wall which restrains the natural flow of waters and results in the redirecting of said waters onto the road surface of any county right-of-way within the county.
(5) The term "damage" does not include normal wear and tear to county rights-of-way from use of such rights-of-way by an operator in the course of transporting timber or pulpwood harvested in the county.
(6) The term "damage" does not include damage to county rights-of-way built with inadequate drainage or other features not in conformance with state standards.
Enforcement officer means the county sheriff, the county road superintendent, or their deputies, marshals, constables, or designees.
Landowner means any person, entity, individual, partnership, corporation, association or other organization, including the officers, agents and employees thereof owning land in the county.
Operator means any person, entity, individual, partnership, corporation, association or other organization, including the officers, agents and employees thereof carrying out the activities contemplated by this article.
Permit holder means a successful applicant.
Repair means the repair of a county right-of-way to its condition prior to the occurrence of damage caused by transporting timber or pulpwood harvested in the county.
Rights-of-way means the shoulder, front slope, ditch, drain, and back slope of a county road.
Violation means operating without a permit or when a permit has been revoked.
( Ord. No. 01092002 , § III, 1-8-2002)
287:
It shall be unlawful for any operator engaged in transporting timber or pulpwood over county rights-of-way to damage county rights-of-way of the county.
( Ord. No. 01092002 , § IV, 1-8-2002)
288:
On and after January 9, 2002, no operator shall access county rights-of-way in the county incident to timber or pulpwood harvesting without first obtaining a permit.
( Ord. No. 01092002 , § V, 1-8-2002)
289:
For each permit sought pursuant to this article, the applicant shall pay a fee the in amounts as determined by the board of commissioners from time to time payable to the county.
( Ord. No. 01092002 , § VI, 1-8-2002)
290:
(a) In addition to any other requirements imposed under this article, no applicant shall be issued an access permit unless a bond has been procured in accordance with this section for access to county rights-of-way.
(b) The bond for an access permit applicant shall be $2,500.00.
(c) Only one bond shall be required by an applicant to satisfy the requirements of this section regardless of the number of access permits applied for or in effect. Said bond shall remain in effect so long as covered operations are being conducted by the applicant in the county.
( Ord. No. 01092002 , § VII, 1-8-2002)
291:
(a) An access permit may be obtained upon application to the county road superintendent by the applicant seeking to transport timber or pulpwood harvested in the county.
(b) The applicant must provide an accurate description of the property from which the timber or pulpwood is to be transported, and the permit shall only be valid for that particular operation. The applicant must also show proof of the bond required by this article. In addition, the applicant must give an estimate for the approximate time of commencement and completion of the operation, the name and address of the contractor and the property owner, and the name and address of the person who shall be in charge of, or shall act in a supervisory capacity over, the operations. The county must issue the access permit within three business days of application.
(c) The county board of tax assessors shall be notified by the county road superintendent as to each access permit issued pursuant to this article.
( Ord. No. 01092002 , § VIII, 1-8-2002)
292:
(a) Rights-of-way. The use of the county rights-of-way by an operator transporting timber or pulpwood must not endanger the traveling public; where damage does occur, the rights-of-way so damaged shall be restored to their previous condition, provided that the rights-of-way were constructed and maintained to state standards, including, but not limited to, removal of debris and mud and replacement of gravel. Transportation equipment shall not be allowed to park on public rights-of-way for extended amounts of time.
(b) Signs. An operator transporting timber or pulpwood over county rights-of-way shall post at least one sign in each direction from the entrance onto the road used by the operator to alert motorists. The signs should be placed in locations visible to oncoming traffic between 500 and 1,000 feet on either side of the road entrance. Each sign should be orange with dimensions of at least 24 inches by 24 inches and should read "Caution Trucks Entering Highway" or an equivalent message.
(c) Termination. At the termination of permitted activities at each permitted site, an operator shall immediately notify the road superintendent who shall make an inspection of the county rights-of-way affected by the proposed activities. The inspection shall take place within three business days of receipt of said notice.
(d) Results of inspection/appeal/release. If the inspection required by subsection (c) of this section results in a finding that no damage occurred, the superintendent shall immediately notify the applicant. The bond shall be released at the permit holder's discretion upon said notification. In the event damage has occurred, the applicant having caused the damage shall undertake the repairs necessary to return the county road or right-of-way to its original condition. If there is disagreement with the road superintendent's assessment that damage has occurred, the applicant may appeal the decision of the road superintendent to the county manager/administrator. An adverse decision of the county manager/administrator may subsequently be appealed by the applicant to the county governing authority. Note: If there is no county manager or administrator, the initial appeal is to the county governing authority.
(e) Repairs by county. In the event no appeal is filed, or appeals have been decided against permit holder, and the permit holder responsible has not effectuated the repairs, the road superintendent shall be authorized to use county labor, equipment, and materials to restore to the county rights-of-way to their prior condition in which event the county shall be authorized to draw against the bond in an amount necessary to reimburse county for all expenses incurred as a result of said repairs.
